paragraphs.text: Measure what your system prompt is made of, and put the operating protocol ahead of the rule block.
# dsh-prompt-balance

Measure what your system prompt is actually made of — then make sure the model reads the
operating p
rotocol before it reads the prohibitions.
Works on DeepSeek Harness (DSH). Two hooks, no build step, no dependencies.
## The problem

Long-running agents accumulate rules: an `AGENTS.md` that grew to 65 KB, a workspace
policy, a templ

ate guide, a data-security annex. Nobody measures the result. In one real
case the breakdown was **6

5% rules / 10.7% identity** — the model's first screen of text was
fourteen kilobytes of "don't", al

most nothing about who it was working for or what good work
looked like.
Two consequences follow:

1. You cannot argue about prompt quality without numbers. "My prompt feels bloated" is not
actionabl

e; "rules are 42,331 bytes of 64,902, and they sit first" is.
2. Order matters. Instructions near th

e front of the assembly carry more weight than the
same instructions buried after a wall of constrai

ont of the assembly carry more weight than the
same instructions buried after a wall of constraints.
## What it does
| Hook | Effect |
| `system-prompt/assemble` | Writes every section's byte size to `~/.dsh/prompt-balance.log`, then p
repends one short `<operator-protocol>` block **before** all rule sections. Idempotent: it will not

stack a second gate. |
| `agent/pre-step` | `AGENTS.md` arrives as an ordinary message, so context c
ompression treats it as history and can summarize the specifics away. This hook prefixes a ~250-byte
identity digest so the "who am I serving" frame survives the fold. |

## Configure — this is the part that matters

Out of the box the identity block is a placeholder. The gate only earns its keep when it
names a rea
l person doing real work. Create `~/.dsh/prompt-balance.json`:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Both keys are optional and independent:
- `identity` — a string array, joined with newlines. Used in the gate **and** in the pre-step digest

.
- `gate` — a string array. First line is the framing sentence, the rest are the numbered checks.

Delete the file to return to defaults. Nothing else in the plugin is configurable, and it
never writ

return to defaults. Nothing else in the plugin is configurable, and it
never writes to your config.
## What you get in the log
[代码示例省略，未执行]

`in`/`out`/`gate` are byte counts, so you can prove the cost of the gate itself. `rules` is
the sum

of sections whose names match `instruction|agents|workspace|memory|rule`; if your
host names its sec
tions differently, that number is meaningless — read the `top=` list instead.
## Compatibility

- DSH kernel `0.2.1-rc.*` and later. Verified against `@deepseek-ai/dsh-system-prompt`
`lib/index.js

:398` — the waterfall passes `(assembly, context, next)`, three parameters.
A handler declared with

four parameters throws `next is not a function` and takes every
tool call down with it; this plugin

declares three.
- Node 20+. No runtime dependencies.
- Nothing throws at import time: a failed loade

r entry makes the desktop app show its
recovery dialog, so every step is wrapped and reported to the

the desktop app show its
recovery dialog, so every step is wrapped and reported to the log instead.
## Uninstall
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The log file stays at `~/.dsh/prompt-balance.log`; delete it yourself if you want it gone.
